question.text: A BIPA (Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement) protects foreign investors by:

answer.text: Protecting against repatriation risks and arbitration risks in case of hostilities between countries, and providing investment incentives
Exempting them from all Indian taxes

explanation.text: The Logic: BIPA is a jurisdiction-selection factor that helps protect foreign investors' financial interests in India in case of hostilities between countries, repatriation risks, and arbitration risks, and it also covers investment incentives. Offshore investors therefore consider BIPA coverage when choosing the jurisdiction through which they invest into India. The Trap: BIPA provides legal and investment protections — it does not guarantee returns, fund performance, or exemption from Indian tax. It is about safeguarding the investment, not about profitability. Note: BIPA coverage is one of the jurisdiction-selection factors offshore investors consider alongside DTAA benefits, regulatory regime, and ease of capital repatriation.
